title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 71
paragraphs: Now those of the Athenians who were “under the curse” got this name as follows. There was a certain Cylon among the Athenians, a man who had been victorious at the Olympic games. He behaved arrogantly, wishing to make himself tyrant; and having formed for himself an association of men of his own age, he tried to seize the Acropolis. Not being able to take it, he sat as a suppliant before the image of the goddess. These men were taken from their place as suppliants by the presidents of the naucraries, who at that time administered affairs at Athens, on the condition that they should be liable to any penalty short of death; and the Alcmaeonidae were accused of having put them to death. This had happened before the time of Peisistratus.
